CausalChain: Lysosomal pH modulation -> impaired NCOA4-mediated ferritinophagy -> reduced ferritin degradation -> lower labile iron pool -> diminished Fenton reaction -> decreased lipid peroxidation -> reduced ferroptosis in hepatocytes -> mitigation of liver injury
Hypothesis: Modulating lysosomal pH to impair ferritinophagy in hepatocytes will decrease labile iron accumulation and oxidative lipid damage, thereby protecting against ferroptosis-driven liver injury in conditions such as ischemia–reperfusion and drug-induced liver damage.
Abstract: We propose that targeted modulation of lysosomal pH in hepatocytes can serve as a novel strategy to reduce ferroptosis-induced liver injury. By mildly alkalinizing the lysosomal environment, the degradation of ferritin via NCOA4‐mediated ferritinophagy may be impaired, leading to a reduction in the labile iron pool. This decrease in free iron limits the Fenton reaction and subsequent lipid peroxidation, thereby attenuating ferroptotic cell death. This hypothesis, if validated, could open new therapeutic avenues for protection against ischemia–reperfusion injury, drug-induced liver injury, and progression of chronic liver diseases.
